correctness.rationale: The 11-bit temporal-column equation is a bijection between time-eleven fixed ring states and length-n closed walks of the explicit \(2^{22}\)-state deterministic spatial map. Exact independent full-state functional traversal and indegree peel both find exactly one spatial cycle of each length 1, 2, 143, 275. Direct Rule 30 simulation validates both nonconstant witness words as primitive temporal eleven and spatially primitive. Since eleven is prime, subtracting time-fixed states and dividing by eleven proves \(C_{11}(n)=13\mathbf 1_{143\mid n}+25\mathbf 1_{275\mid n}\). Explicit finite-state certificate is included; no infinite claim is inferred from short ring enumeration.

value.rationale: Sharp minimal spatial size for an exact temporal eleven-cycle in a canonical chaotic cellular automaton is a natural, externally motivated invariant. The new \(143\)-site witness reduces a printed \(275\)-site requirement, while the complete classification identifies the only two primitive spatial families and exact \(13\)- and \(25\)- temporal orbit contributions on every circumference. A complete all-n classification is not a trivial re-expression of one computed example and serves as a precise benchmark for Rule 30 recurrence.
